question: When are you most likely to hook an inpatient up to a portable monitor?

options.A: During intrahospital transport to diagnostic imaging
options.B: While the patient is sleeping quietly in a stable hospital bed
options.C: During routine discharge education in the room
options.D: When filing physical paper records in the nurses' station

explanation: Whenever we roll a patient out of their room for an X-ray or scan (diagnostic imaging), we hook them up to a portable monitor to keep them safe on the journey. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T10#GNS212_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant mothers about good nutrition during antenatal care?

options.A: To help the mother lose weight during the first trimester
options.B: To guarantee a completely painless labor and delivery
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine blood pressure checks
options.D: To prevent low birth weight and support fetal development

explanation: You've got this! Proper nutrition is key to helping the baby grow strong and healthy while keeping the mother in great shape throughout her pregnancy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h1)

question: What is the best way to get nursing staff to happily accept and use new hospital software?

options.A: Punishing nurses who express frustration or make mistakes during the transition
options.B: Involving frontline nurses in the software selection and workflow design process
options.C: Replacing all computers with paper charts if the first day of training is difficult
options.D: Requiring staff to figure out the new computer program entirely on their own

explanation: When bedside nurses help choose and test the software from the start, the system actually fits everyday hospital needs and is much easier to use. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)

question: What does having an 'ability-focused mindset' mean for the healthcare team?

options.A: What the client is still able to do
options.B: The permanent deficits caused by the injury
options.C: How fast the client can be discharged home
options.D: Only the laboratory test results

explanation: Instead of focusing on what a patient has lost, an ability-focused mindset looks at their remaining strengths to build their confidence. Spotting strengths is a great nursing skill! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h2)

question: If a patient misses work for weeks due to a hospital admission, how is their lost salary classified?

options.A: Indirect cost
options.B: Capital cost
options.C: Intangible cost
options.D: Direct medical cost

explanation: Indirect costs happen because illness stops someone from working. The hospital bill is direct, but the lost salary at their job is an indirect cost. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do we need to turn heavy research data into quick clinical guidelines for bedside nurses?

options.A: Guidelines replace the need for critical thinking in patient care
options.B: Bedside nurses are not allowed to look at original research data
options.C: Hospital policies forbid nurses from talking about academic studies
options.D: Clinicians rarely have time to read lengthy, complex research papers

explanation: Spot on! Busy clinical nurses are always on their feet and need quick, easy-to-digest summaries rather than long academic manuscripts. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h5)

question: What term describes the use of multiple medications simultaneously, which is common in older adults?

options.A: Enteric coating
options.B: Polypharmacy
options.C: Aspiration risk
options.D: First-pass effect

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the concurrent use of multiple drugs by a patient, which frequently happens in geriatric care and raises the risk of drug interactions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why do many developing countries often need external health support and international aid?

options.A: Private hospitals refuse to treat patients without foreign backing
options.B: International donors legally mandate that local taxes be abolished
options.C: Government health budgets often fall short of recommended funding targets
options.D: Citizens prefer foreign organizations over government clinics

explanation: When national funding isn't enough to cover public health needs, external donations step in to help keep clinics open and running. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h1)

question: How do computers help nurses manage vital signs and patient numbers?

options.A: By following programmed steps to turn raw numbers into useful information
options.B: By making independent medical diagnoses using intuition
options.C: By storing information permanently without electricity
options.D: By turning handwritten notes into paper charts

explanation: Computers don't think like humans do! They rely on smart programming to turn raw numbers into clear, meaningful information for your shift. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is a common ethical worry when patients use modern smart assistive devices?

options.A: Loss of personal privacy through continuous health data collection
options.B: Excessive face-to-face interaction with hospital staff
options.C: Immediate destruction of all electronic health records
options.D: Uncontrolled increases in physical nursing workloads

explanation: Correct! Smart devices often track daily movements and health stats, which raises real questions about keeping patient data private. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which eye condition means a patient should NEVER take anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Narrow-angle glaucoma
options.B: Color blindness
options.C: Simple conjunctivitis
options.D: Cataracts of the lens

explanation: Anticholinergics can trap fluid inside the eye and cause a dangerous spike in pressure for glaucoma patients. Always check this history! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h6)

question: How are benign tumors different from malignant ones?

options.A: Benign tumors cannot grow larger than a few millimeters.
options.B: Benign tumors only occur in the blood and lymphatic system.
options.C: Benign tumors do not invade nearby tissues or spread to distant sites.
options.D: Benign tumors consist of dead cells rather than dividing cells.

explanation: Think of benign tumors as staying put in one place without invading surrounding tissues. They aren't cancerous like malignant ones! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h1)

question: What is an essential part of nursing counseling when a couple chooses a traditional family planning method?

options.A: Telling them that partner involvement is unnecessary
options.B: Insisting they switch immediately to surgical sterilization
options.C: Prohibiting them from asking questions about modern drugs
options.D: Discussing the higher risk of failure and backup options

explanation: Good counseling means making sure clients know how well a method actually works so they can plan ahead if a mistake happens. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h8)

question: Which organization sets the rules and scope of practice for nurses right here in Nigeria?

options.A: World Health Organization Africa
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Information
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: That's the NMCN! They guide our training, exams, and professional practice across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h4)

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why is allowing residents to make their own choices (autonomy) so important in long-term care?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision
options.B: It accelerates the natural healing of acute infections
options.C: It helps preserve resident dignity and psychological health
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of running the facility

explanation: Spot on! When people can still make choices about their day, it boosts their self-worth and keeps their spirits high. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why is giving incorrect drug information a serious ethical and legal mistake for a nurse?

options.A: It prevents the pharmaceutical company from selling more medications
options.B: It takes too much time away from routine ward cleaning duties
options.C: It can directly harm the patient and violates the professional duty of care
options.D: It lowers the overall financial revenue of the hospital pharmacy

explanation: You got it! Our primary duty is to protect our patients from harm, which means we must always provide accurate drug guidance. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why must patients finish their entire course of antibiotics even after they start feeling better?

options.A: To prevent the medication from expiring in the home cabinet
options.B: To guarantee the patient gains healthy weight during recovery
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy gets paid for the full prescription amount
options.D: To prevent the survival and growth of resistant bacterial strains

explanation: Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive. They can multiply back stronger, leading to drug-resistant infections that are hard to treat. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the difference between data fabrication and data falsification?

options.A: Fabrication applies to nursing, falsification applies to physics
options.B: Fabrication is inventing fake data, while falsification is altering real data
options.C: Fabrication is legal with IRB approval, falsification is never allowed
options.D: Fabrication is stealing text, falsification is stealing money

explanation: You got it! Fabrication means making numbers up from thin air, while falsification means tampering with real results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h7)

question: Why is telehealth particularly helpful for patients living in remote rural areas?

options.A: It replaces the need for any electrical power in the home
options.B: It reduces the need to travel long distances for routine check-ins
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never need surgery
options.D: It makes prescription drugs free for everyone

explanation: Telehealth lets patients consult nurses and doctors remotely, saving travel time and expenses for those far from health facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why are research instruments compared to clinical tools like a thermometer?

options.A: They both need precision to capture accurate information.
options.B: They are both disposable after a single patient use.
options.C: They are both used exclusively in hospital emergency rooms.
options.D: They both require electricity to function properly.

explanation: Just as a thermometer must be accurate to measure body heat, a research instrument must be precise to capture true data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the meeting point between the ectocervix and the endocervical canal called?

options.A: The myometrial junction
options.B: The fundal attachment
options.C: The transformation zone
options.D: The pelvic floor arch

explanation: Spot on! It's called the transformation zone—a busy area where different types of cells meet and undergo active changes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when collecting data?

options.A: Training all data collectors thoroughly before starting
options.B: Securing formal institutional approvals from management
options.C: Pilot testing questionnaires on a small sample group
options.D: Discarding digital backups immediately to save storage space

explanation: You nailed it! Deleting your backups is a huge risk that can lead to permanent data loss—definitely something we want to avoid! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h7)

question: How do traditional food taboos negatively affect community health?

options.A: They cause farmers to grow only cash crops instead of edible vegetables
options.B: They prevent vulnerable groups like pregnant women from eating nutrient-dense foods
options.C: They force families to spend all their income on expensive imported foods
options.D: They make the soil too acidic for crops like beans and maize to grow

explanation: You nailed it. Cultural rules often keep protein-rich foods away from the pregnant women and children who need them the most. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: Why is a predictable daily routine important in a half-way house?

options.A: It promotes stability and reduces anxiety for residents
options.B: It replaces the need for any medication or therapy
options.C: It ensures that nurses have less paperwork to complete
options.D: It punishes residents who wake up late in the morning

explanation: Great thinking! Structure and predictability help individuals with mental health conditions feel secure, calm, and organized. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h5)

question: How would you best describe Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)?

options.A: A degenerative muscular disease
options.B: A lifelong neurodevelopmental condition
options.C: A preventable infectious illness
options.D: A temporary childhood behavioral phase

explanation: You've got this! Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition, meaning it stays with a person throughout their entire life. It's just a different way of experiencing the world. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h1)

question: What do we call nutrients that our bodies cannot make on their own, so we must get them from our food?

options.A: Secondary metabolites
options.B: Synthetic polymers
options.C: Endogenous proteins
options.D: Essential nutrients

explanation: Spot on! Essential nutrients are the ones your body can't manufacture by itself, so eating them is a must for survival. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h1)

question: What does "interdependence" mean in a community?

options.A: The government controls every aspect of private family life
options.B: Members and subgroups rely on each other for survival and support
options.C: Foreign countries manage all local health clinics
options.D: Every single household produces all its own food and medicine

explanation: Interdependence means people and groups lean on one another to make daily life work smoothly. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why should a 38-year-old client who gets migraines with aura avoid combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: It triggers severe allergic skin rashes on the face
options.B: It will cause her migraines to happen every single day
options.C: It significantly increases her risk of having a stroke
options.D: It stops the migraine medication from working properly

explanation: This is a classic safety rule in pharmacology: migraines with aura, plus estrogen, plus being over 35 multiplies the risk of a dangerous stroke. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h3)

question: After teaching a patient about wound care, what must the nurse document in the patient's notes?

options.A: Nothing, as verbal education does not require charting
options.B: Details of what was taught, the method used, and the patient's response
options.C: A summary of the nurse's personal feelings about the patient
options.D: Only the date and the nurse's personal signature

explanation: Well done! If it wasn't charted, legally it wasn't done. Always record what you taught and how the patient responded. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the term for cancer cells spreading to distant parts of the body?

options.A: Metastasis
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Angiogenesis
options.D: Differentiation

explanation: Metastasis occurs when malignant cells break free, enter circulation or lymph channels, and establish secondary tumor sites far from the original growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important to let the nurse share their side of the story during an investigation?

options.A: To ensure fairness and uncover any misunderstood details
options.B: To trick the nurse into admitting a bigger crime
options.C: To let the nurse write the final company policies
options.D: To delay the disciplinary process indefinitely

explanation: Listening to the employee provides a complete picture, ensuring management does not act on incomplete information. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for spreading an epidemic in a community?

options.A: High vaccination coverage
options.B: Poor solid waste management
options.C: Overcrowded living conditions
options.D: Inadequate clean water supply

explanation: Spot on! High vaccination coverage actually protects a community and stops disease spread, making it the correct exception here. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h4)

question: Which simple tool does a community health nurse use to listen to the baby's heartbeat during a home visit?

options.A: A sphygmomanometer
options.B: An ophthalmoscope
options.C: A percussion hammer
options.D: A Pinard stethoscope

explanation: A Pinard stethoscope (or portable Doppler) is your trusty companion in the field for checking fetal heart tones! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T4#GNS225_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do nurses also view groups living far apart as a 'community' if they share a common bond?

options.A: Because government funding requires international grouping
options.B: Because modern hospitals treat all patients as a single population
options.C: Because physical geography has no impact on human health outcomes
options.D: Because they experience similar health challenges and support needs

explanation: Spot on! Even if people live in different towns, groups like nursing mothers or people with sickle cell share similar health needs that nurses can help support together. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T1#GNS225_U1_T1_h1)

question: A CT scan image shows a cross-section of the abdomen dividing it into top and bottom halves. Which plane was used?

options.A: Transverse
options.B: Sagittal
options.C: Midsagittal
options.D: Coronal

explanation: Think of slicing a loaf of bread! Cross-sections that view the body from top to bottom are produced by cutting along the transverse plane. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h3)

question: A researcher studies whether a new walking program lowers blood pressure in elderly patients. What is the dependent variable?

options.A: Blood pressure level
options.B: The researcher conducting the study
options.C: The walking program
options.D: The age of the elderly patients

explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome being measured, which in this case is the patient's blood pressure responding to the exercise. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these practices is NOT part of safe umbilical cord care taught by nurses?

options.A: Applying animal dung to stop bleeding
options.B: Using a sterile blade to cut the cord
options.C: Washing hands thoroughly before handling the cord
options.D: Keeping the cord stump dry and uncovered

explanation: Spot on! Putting things like animal dung or ash on the cord introduces tetanus spores and must always be avoided. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h8)

question: What does the term 'fidelity' mean when talking about healthcare simulators?

options.A: How easily the simulator can be moved between classrooms
options.B: How closely the simulation mimics a real-life clinical situation
options.C: How much the simulator costs to purchase and maintain
options.D: How many students can use the simulator at the same time

explanation: Fidelity describes the level of realism and how well the simulation copies actual patient care scenarios. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h2)

question: You are the first nurse to arrive at an accident scene and you notice a strong smell of leaking gas. What is your very first step?

options.A: Wait inside the ambulance until police complete all paperwork.
options.B: Run immediately to pull victims out of the wreckage.
options.C: Ensure personal safety and environmental security before entering.
options.D: Begin chest compressions on the nearest injured person.

explanation: Safety first! If you rush in and become a victim yourself, you can't help anyone. Always check that the environment is safe before stepping in. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the name of the special agency established in 1987 to drive primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Rural Hospital Construction Board
options.B: West African Nursing and Midwifery Council
options.C: Federal Ministry of Tertiary Education and Health
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: Nigeria established the NPHCDA in 1987 to coordinate and strengthen primary health care delivery across the country. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the condition called when the placenta implants low in the uterus and covers the cervix?

options.A: Placenta accreta
options.B: Succenturiate placenta
options.C: Placenta previa
options.D: Circumvallate placenta

explanation: You'll encounter this often in clinicals: 'previa' means the placenta gets in the way by sitting right over or near the cervical opening. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h7)

question: When a community health nurse speaks up for marginalized villagers who lack clean water, what nursing role is being demonstrated?

options.A: Pharmacologist
options.B: Surgeon
options.C: Advocate
options.D: Administrator

explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up, defending, and fighting for the rights and health needs of vulnerable or voiceless populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: When we talk about 'local sources of nutrients' in Nigerian diets, what do we mainly mean?

options.A: Processed canned foods found in international supermarkets
options.B: Synthetic vitamins manufactured in laboratory settings
options.C: Foods grown and harvested within a community or country
options.D: Expensive dietary supplements imported from overseas

explanation: Spot on! Local nutrient sources are simply the foods naturally grown and produced right here in our environment or nation. It makes eating healthy much more practical! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T007#GNS227_U3_T007_h1)

question: Why is the community health planning cycle a continuous loop instead of a straight line?

options.A: Nurses must repeat the exact same paperwork every single month
options.B: Evaluation findings feed back into new assessments to improve future care
options.C: Health problems never change once an intervention is finished
options.D: It stops the community from ever joining in on healthcare

explanation: Exactly! Healthcare doesn't stop. What you learn from evaluating a project helps you plan even better care for the next round. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: In traditional Nigerian societies, what was usually believed to be the main cause of severe mental illness?

options.A: Degeneration of brain cells from aging
options.B: A deficiency of essential dietary vitamins
options.C: Spiritual forces and ancestral influences
options.D: Genetic mutations passed down generations

explanation: Spot on! Historically, communities often connected deep emotional or psychological struggles to spiritual factors, witchcraft, or broken taboos rather than biological causes. You've got this! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h1)

question: How often should you turn an immobile patient to protect their skin from pressure sores?

options.A: At least every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Only when the family asks
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Turning patients every two hours lets blood flow back into pressed skin, stopping pressure injuries before they start. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h7)

question: In research, what does a standard p-value of 0.05 mean?

options.A: The researcher made a calculation mistake 5 times during the test
options.B: There is a 5 percent probability the results happened by chance
options.C: 95 percent of the patients dropped out before the study ended
options.D: The intervention was successful in exactly 5 out of 100 hospitals

explanation: Exactly! A p-value of 0.05 means there's only a 1 in 20 chance that your exciting results are just a fluke. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h4)

question: How can rude or harsh behavior by staff at a receiving hospital negatively affect the referral system?

options.A: It discourages patients and their relatives from seeking formal care in the future
options.B: It improves communication between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: It makes patients recover faster because they want to leave early
options.D: It encourages villagers to build more primary health care centers

explanation: Negative attitudes create a hostile environment, causing patients to avoid hospitals and patronize unqualified providers instead. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is a major risk to a newborn if the mother receives strong pain opioids right before delivery?

options.A: Neonatal respiratory depression
options.B: Rapid premature bone growth
options.C: Severe congenital heart defects
options.D: Permanent hearing impairment

explanation: If opioids cross the placenta just before birth, the baby might be born a bit too sleepy to take a good first breath on their own. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is a main difference between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Personal goals focus on individual growth, while organisational goals focus on collective institutional success
options.B: Personal goals never involve learning or professional development
options.C: Personal goals are always written by the government, while organisational goals are written by nurses
options.D: Organisational goals only care about individual staff salaries

explanation: Think of it simply: personal goals are about your own growth and pocket, while organisational goals are about the success and health standards of the whole hospital. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Mild joint stiffness
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Benign skin rashes
options.D: Common seasonal influenza

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the top dangers new mothers face globally. Knowing how to manage it is key for every nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: What is the difference between vulnerability and capacity in a disaster setting?

options.A: Vulnerability is an administrative hospital term, while capacity is an emergency field nursing term
options.B: Vulnerability describes weaknesses that make people susceptible to harm, while capacity describes resources available to manage risk
options.C: Vulnerability refers exclusively to financial debt, while capacity refers strictly to building structures
options.D: Vulnerability is measured only after a disaster, while capacity is measured before any hazard appears

explanation: Vulnerability means what makes us prone to suffering (like weak buildings or lack of shelter), while capacity is our strength and resources to fight back! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do drugs like sildenafil fail to work if the patient lacks sexual stimulation?

options.A: They are digested too quickly by stomach acid without excitement
options.B: They require the physical presence of a medical doctor to activate
options.C: They only enhance the natural signaling pathway triggered by arousal
options.D: They act purely as sedatives for the nervous system

explanation: Pau-cle! These medications don't cause automatic arousal on their own; they simply boost the body's natural blood flow response when stimulation is already there. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T27#GNS312_U1_T27_h5)

question: Where is the insular lobe located within the brain?

options.A: At the very back of the skull
options.B: Deep inside the lateral sulcus
options.C: Right behind the forehead bones
options.D: On the outer surface of the temples

explanation: The insula is buried deep within the lateral sulcus, hidden beneath the other overlying lobes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h6)

question: What is the main goal of the Model for Improvement in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the total number of administrative reports filled out daily
options.B: To replace traditional nursing judgment with computer algorithms
options.C: To help clinical teams make practical changes that improve patient outcomes
options.D: To punish staff members who make mistakes during patient care

explanation: You got this! The model is simply a guide to help healthcare workers make meaningful, tested changes that make patient care better every day. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do modern burn teams rush to surgically remove dead burn tissue (eschar) early on?

options.A: It removes dead tissue that serves as a breeding ground for infection.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent skin grafting procedures.
options.C: It immediately restores full sensory nerve function to the area.
options.D: It prevents the systemic release of inflammatory cytokines forever.

explanation: Dead skin (eschar) is like a feast for bacteria. Getting rid of it early stops severe infections and gets the wound ready for a healthy graft. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h6)

question: What does 'rational drug use' mean for a patient?

options.A: Every patient leaves the clinic with at least five different prescriptions
options.B: Patients receive the right drug, correct dose, and proper duration for their condition
options.C: Doctors prescribe the most expensive medication available on the market
options.D: Pharmacies clear out all their expiring stock within forty-eight hours

explanation: You got it! Rational use means matching the exact illness with a safe, cost-effective treatment without waste or misuse. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why might two teenagers of the exact same age look and grow quite differently?

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a newly introduced nursing practice?

question: Where do most nutrient pollutants like nitrogen and phosphorus in water bodies come from?

options.C: Agricultural fertilizer runoff
options.D: Floating physical plastic waste

question: Why must a nurse carefully check blood compatibility before starting a blood transfusion?

options.B: To ensure the donor red blood cells do not dissolve in normal saline

question: Why are pure opioid agonists like morphine considered strong pain relievers?

options.C: They eliminate all inflammation directly at the injury site.

question: Which modern lab technique identifies germs by copying and checking their unique genetic code?

question: An emergency ward is trying out a new documentation tool. What action will best help the staff adopt it successfully?

question: What is the main goal of using skull traction for someone with a neck injury?

options.A: To align and stabilize damaged cervical vertebrae

options.C: To deliver intravenous pain medication directly to the neck
options.D: To increase blood flow to the brain tissues

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge currently facing the nursing profession worldwide?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Complete elimination of all patient illnesses
options.C: Shortages of qualified nursing personnel
options.D: High rates of workplace stress and burnout

question: Which of these is a common task for a nurse when dealing with patient insurance?

question: What is the most important immediate nursing action after a fasting blood draw for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Provide food and allow the patient to take held morning medications.

options.C: Instruct the patient to continue fasting until the lab results return.

question: What makes Evidence-Based Practice (EBP) broader than just research utilization?

question: When is the best time to use a multiple line graph?

question: What is 'click fatigue' in the context of electronic health records?

options.A: Physical hand cramps caused by holding a computer mouse too tightly
options.B: Spending excessive time navigating confusing menus and clicking through screens
options.C: A battery failure in wireless barcode scanners during night shifts
options.D: Eye strain from staring at bright computer monitors all day

question: What is the main job of an Institutional Review Board (IRB)?

options.B: To market new medical products to the public
options.C: To protect the rights and safety of human research subjects
options.D: To write nursing textbooks for universities

question: A nurse manager wants to reduce medication handover delays. What is the best action during the Plan phase?

question: What is a key visual difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

question: A cook uses the same chopping board for raw chicken and fresh tomatoes without washing it first. What just happened?

explanation: Using dirty equipment between raw meat and fresh veggies easily transfers bacteria from one to the other. Spot on! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h2)

question: When does a community health financing scheme achieve true efficiency?

options.A: When it reduces the number of nurses working in rural clinics
options.B: When it charges higher fees for emergency services
options.C: When it maximizes health benefits from available resources without waste
options.D: When it stops purchasing essential drugs to save money

explanation: Efficiency is all about getting the best possible health outcomes out of limited funds without wasting valuable resources. Great job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a mandatory safety action when a newborn is receiving phototherapy?

question: Which of these everyday activities is a classic example of NEAT (Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis)?

question: What is the primary goal of home care for patients with chronic illnesses?

options.C: Achieving total disease cure within one week

question: Why is it smart to involve bedside nurses when drafting new unit objectives?

question: Which method do nurses usually use to gather health facts directly from a community?

question: Why do we need water-soluble vitamins in our diet almost every day?

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the main reason for using the Z-track technique during an IM injection?

question: Why does blood pressure fall in early and mid-pregnancy even though blood volume is rising?

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

question: What is the primary purpose of an after-action review (AAR) following a disaster?

question: What is the main job of a social worker on a community health team?

question: What is a common resource barrier faced by nurses trying to maintain quality care in Nigeria?

question: What is the main benefit of using a Food Frequency Questionnaire?

question: How can nurse managers prevent staff from feeling overwhelmed by MBO?

question: Why must gloves be removed before taking off the isolation gown during doffing?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when planning an IEC activity?

question: What stimulates the kidneys to release erythropoietin (EPO)?

question: Which of these is an example of an institutional barrier to immunization?

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) rank when we talk about safety controls?

question: Why does the National Essential Medicines List divide drugs by levels of healthcare (like PHCs vs teaching hospitals)?

question: A patient says, 'My life is completely useless.' The nurse replies, 'You feel that your life has no meaning right now?' What communication skill is this?

question: Why is it smart for nurses to involve local community leaders in mental health programs?

question: As a nurse, what is an important rule to remember when checking in on a traumatized patient?

question: A pregnant woman in your community presents with a rigid, painful tummy and dark bleeding. What is the most likely cause?

question: What is the best immediate nursing action for an unconscious patient who is breathing on their own?

question: What is the main job of smallholder farmers in local food systems?

question: When is a newborn baby usually most awake and ready to try breastfeeding for the very first time?

question: When studying community health, what does 'incidence' mainly measure?

question: A heavy rainstorm destroys homes in a rural village. Which local group is in the best position to take immediate action first?

options.C: The Federal Ministry of Aviation
options.D: Local Emergency Management Committees

explanation: Local committees are right there in the community, making them the fastest first responders on the ground before higher agencies arrive. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h3)

question: How should nurses and doctors communicate with a family after an adverse event?

options.A: By avoiding the patient room entirely until the issue is forgotten

options.C: By blaming the hospital cafeteria for causing the clinical error
options.D: With honesty, empathy, and clear explanations without medical jargon

explanation: Families appreciate the truth delivered with a compassionate heart and plain, simple words they can easily understand. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: At what point during your shift should you separate hospital waste?

options.C: After all waste is mixed together in the utility room
options.D: At the exact moment and place of generation

question: Where does active skin cell division take place in the outer layer (epidermis)?

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the milk ejection or let-down reflex?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen

options.D: Oxytocin

question: Which dimension of healthcare quality focuses on preventing injuries from care that is supposed to help?

options.A: Safe care
options.B: Efficient care
options.C: Equitable care
options.D: Timely care

explanation: Spot on! Keeping patients safe means protecting them from accidental harm or injuries while they are receiving treatment in our care. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which stage of wastewater treatment relies mainly on physical screening and letting solids settle?

options.B: Secondary treatment
options.C: Quaternary treatment

question: A student nurse uses old patient admission files from last year to study malaria rates. What kind of data source is this?

options.A: Subjective data source
options.B: Secondary data source
options.C: Primary data source
options.D: Experimental data source

explanation: Because someone else collected those files in the past, you are using a secondary source. It's like hand-me-down data! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h2)

question: A nursing researcher states: 'To examine if handwashing frequency reduces hospital-acquired infections.' What is this statement?

options.A: A research objective
options.B: A data collection tool
options.C: A research hypothesis
options.D: A final study conclusion

explanation: Spotting an action verb like 'to examine' right at the beginning is a dead giveaway that you're looking at a research objective! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why would a patient need a triple-lumen catheter for continuous bladder irrigation?

options.A: It increases the French size automatically during surgery
options.B: It provides separate channels for drainage, balloon inflation, and fluid instillation
options.C: It prevents the patient from accidentally pulling the tube out
options.D: It allows three nurses to flush the bladder simultaneously

explanation: Exactly! Three separate pathways mean fluid can flow in, urine can flow out, and the balloon stays inflated all at the same time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h3)

question: When is the best time to collect a microbiological specimen?

options.A: After the full course of antibiotics is finished
options.B: Twelve hours after stopping all medications
options.C: Before antimicrobial therapy is started
options.D: Immediately after the second dose of antibiotics

explanation: Always collect your sample before starting antibiotics! If the drugs are already in the system, they might kill the germs in the test tube and give you a false negative result. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses often recommend exit alarms or high door locks for homes with a dementia patient?

options.A: To prevent the patient from wandering outside and getting lost
options.B: To keep uninvited guests from entering the compound
options.C: To punish the patient for bad behavior during the day
options.D: To force the patient to stay inside their bedroom at night

explanation: Wandering can be very dangerous because patients easily get disoriented. Simple environmental barriers keep them safe inside. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is a major risk of patients using unverified health websites?

options.A: Their internet connection will permanently stop working
options.B: The hospital will charge extra fees for internet browsing
options.C: They may encounter dangerous misinformation or fake remedies
options.D: Their computer will automatically delete all personal photos

explanation: Unverified sites often lack medical review, leading patients to trust inaccurate or harmful health advice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary medical term for a low salt diet?

options.A: Potassium-depleted diet
options.B: Fluid-restricted diet
options.C: Sodium-restricted diet
options.D: Protein-restricted diet

explanation: A low salt diet is formally called a sodium-restricted diet because it specifically limits sodium intake. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h1)

question: A nurse is getting ready to apply a new fentanyl pain patch to a patient. What important step must be done first?

options.A: Cover the new patch completely with airtight plastic wrap
options.B: Scrub the application site aggressively with surgical soap
options.C: Remove the previous transdermal patch from the patient's skin
options.D: Warm the new patch over a flame to activate the chemicals

question: What does the term 'dual diagnosis' mean in psychiatric care?

options.A: A patient is evaluated by two different doctors on the same day
options.B: A patient has two different physical infections at the same time
options.C: A patient requires two different types of surgical operations
options.D: A patient has both a mental illness and a substance use disorder

question: Which communication tool helps stop a nurse from making wrong assumptions about a patient's home life?

options.A: Relying strictly on family member reports
options.B: Asking open-ended questions
options.C: Avoiding conversation during physical exams
options.D: Using closed-ended yes or no questions

explanation: Spot on! Open questions let patients tell their own stories in their own words without us putting words in their mouths. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for surveillance in developing health systems?

options.A: Having too many computers on every hospital ward
options.B: Too many laboratories producing identical test results
options.C: Shortages of trained laboratory personnel and testing supplies
options.D: Excessive funding that overwhelms the management staff

explanation: Limited resources and trained staff make tracking and confirming infections much harder. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: What do we call the solid ball of about 16 cells formed in the first few days after fertilization?

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?

options.A: Secondary amenorrhea
options.B: Cervical incompetence
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: Which action by a nurse best demonstrates ongoing support for a grieving family after their loved one has passed away?

options.A: Encouraging them to forget the loss and return to work quickly
options.B: Billing the family promptly for grief counseling services
options.C: Sending a sympathy card or making a follow-up phone call weeks later
options.D: Avoiding contact to give them complete isolation

explanation: Small acts of ongoing outreach, such as a card or call, show the family they are remembered and supported through their grief journey. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h8)

question: Why is it best to use short, simple sentences when talking to a patient in a full-blown panic attack?

options.A: Short sentences prevent the nurse from becoming overly anxious as well.
options.B: Patients with panic disorders have difficulty hearing long words.
options.C: Simple sentences make the patient fall asleep immediately.
options.D: Patients in panic have impaired cognitive processing and cannot handle complex information.

explanation: When panic takes over, the brain is flooded with fear and cannot process long explanations. Keep your words brief, clear, and easy to digest. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h7)

question: What is the main goal of doing an occupational health hazard assessment?

options.A: To identify and evaluate potential health and safety risks
options.B: To discipline workers who fail to wear uniforms
options.C: To check the company's financial profits and losses
options.D: To prescribe medications for non-work illnesses

explanation: The main point of a hazard assessment is to spot dangerous conditions early so we can protect workers before anyone gets hurt. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h8)

question: A patient is shy about discussing vaginal dryness. What is the best first thing for a nurse to do?

options.C: Refer her immediately to a psychiatric specialist for mood disorders
options.D: Tell her to wait until her next routine annual physical examination

question: Why is it so important to use simple, everyday language when teaching mothers at the clinic?

options.C: It saves clinic time so the nurse can finish work much earlier
options.D: It guarantees that mothers will memorize the entire clinic manual

question: You hear a call bell ring, but right at that moment, another patient starts struggling to breathe. What should you do first?

options.C: Answer the call bell immediately to find out what is needed

question: What is the best diagnostic test to confirm gout by spotting crystals directly?

options.B: Routine complete blood count with differential
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected limb

question: What is the main benefit of Omega-3 fatty acids for mental health?

options.D: Acting as a direct sedative to induce deep sleep

question: What is the first-line drug treatment for a patient with symptomatic bradycardia?

question: What event triggers the body to start making mature milk in large amounts (Lactogenesis II)?

question: During triage at a disaster scene, which color tag goes to patients who can walk and only have minor cuts or scrapes?

question: What is the main benefit when a family practices subsistence farming?

question: What solution is usually used to clean the skin before inserting the paracentesis needle?

question: What type of consent is assumed when an unconscious trauma patient requires immediate life-saving care?

question: How does health insurance lead to 'moral hazard' in healthcare?

question: What makes an intraarterial line different from a standard intravenous (IV) line?

question: What is the main goal of 'active case finding' during an outbreak?

question: What is the main goal of a sample design in nursing research?

question: If a patient mentions they first visited a traditional or spiritual healer before coming to the hospital, how should a nurse respond?

options.B: Refuse to treat the patient until they sign a formal apology letter

question: What is the daily amount of vegetables recommended to help adults stay healthy?

question: A 48-year-old woman has irregular periods, mood swings, and night sweats over the past year. What stage is she likely in?

question: What turns a bunch of people living close together into a real, active community?

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit with severe trauma. Following the ABCDE approach, what should you check first?

question: A rural health clinic receives a dedicated increase in operational funding. What improvement should the nurse expect to see first?

question: What makes an auto-disable (AD) syringe special?

question: Why do we give emergency epinephrine into the thigh muscle instead of the arm?

question: What usually happens to the price of a medical service when demand for it rises significantly?

question: Why are commercial pastries and doughnuts a bad idea for a patient on a low-fat diet?

question: A nurse is finishing a counselling session by booking a follow-up date and inviting the client back if problems arise. Which GATHER step is this?

question: Which phase of disaster communication focuses primarily on hazard tracking and immediate safety actions?

question: What is the main danger nurses must watch out for in elderly patients undergoing heavy bowel cleansing?

question: What is another common name for Gallows traction?

question: Which muscle in the scrotum wrinkles the skin to keep things warm when the weather is cold?

question: After figuring out how much active medication you need for a dilution, how do you find out how much plain base to add?

question: What is a key feature of how Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF / Doctors Without Borders) operates?

question: Why must drugs chosen for the formulary stay stable in tropical climates?

question: What does accountability mean when a registered nurse delegates a task?

question: Why do we use a positive pressure room for an immunocompromised patient?

explanation: Monitoring watches day-to-day progress, whereas evaluation looks at the final outcomes and overall success of the intervention. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: How does healthy competition ideally affect providers in a free market?

options.A: It forces them to close their doors within a month
options.B: It encourages them to improve quality and manage costs
options.C: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff
options.D: It prevents them from purchasing new technology

explanation: Competition motivates businesses to attract consumers by offering better value, service quality, and efficiency. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h4)

question: What must a unit manager consider when making a fair duty roster?

options.A: Patient acuity and staff skill mix
options.B: The distance of each nurse's house from the hospital
options.C: The personal fashion preferences of nurses
options.D: Only the seniority of the nurses

explanation: Exactly! A good roster looks at how sick the patients are (acuity) and matches them with nurses who have the right skills for the job. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h4)

question: What must a nurse researcher obtain before starting any experiment involving human subjects?

options.A: A grant from a pharmaceutical company
options.B: Ethical approval from a review board
options.C: Approval from local newspaper reporters
options.D: Permission to buy new uniforms

explanation: Patient safety and rights must be protected, so an ethics committee must review and approve the study plan first. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h6)

question: How can you best describe the latent stage of conflict?

options.A: The disagreement is fully resolved and teamwork is restored.
options.B: Individuals realize a problem exists without feeling any emotion.
options.C: Conditions exist for friction, but no dispute has happened yet.
options.D: Staff members are actively yelling at each other in the hallway.

explanation: In the latent stage, the ingredients for a fight are quietly sitting there in the background, but nobody has actually clashed yet. It's the calm before the potential storm. [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h4)

question: On a standard low-fat diet, what is the usual daily upper limit for calories coming from fat?

options.A: More than 60 percent
options.B: Zero percent
options.C: Exactly 50 percent
options.D: Less than 30 percent

explanation: To keep digestion smooth and protect heart health, standard low-fat diets limit total fat to under 30 percent of daily calories. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h1)

question: Why should nurses be careful about relying solely on intuition for patient care?

options.A: It always leads to incorrect clinical decisions
options.B: It is subjective, hard to explain, and prone to personal bias
options.C: It only works for surgical nurses and never for public health nurses
options.D: It is illegal to document gut feelings on a patient chart

explanation: Gut feelings can give you a helpful warning, but they need to be backed up by real, measurable patient assessments. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h4)

question: If you want to know everything a hospitalized patient ate over the past 24 hours, which tool should you use?

options.A: A 24-hour dietary recall
options.B: A complete blood cell count
options.C: A mid-upper arm tape measure
options.D: A serum lipid profile test

explanation: Correct! A 24-hour dietary recall simply has the patient walk you through every single food and drink they had since yesterday. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h7)

question: A clinic nurse notices frequent shortages of basic drugs and sutures. What is a major reason for this in many African nations?

options.A: International agencies ban the importation of basic surgical items
options.B: Nurses generally mismanage the medical supplies in hospital warehouses
options.C: Patients refuse to accept free medications from the government
options.D: National health budgets frequently fall short of the Abuja Declaration target

explanation: When budgets fall short of targets like the Abuja 15%, clinics struggle to buy everyday essentials like gloves, drugs, and suture materials. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h3)

question: What happens in a negative correlation between two variables?

options.A: As one variable increases, the other variable decreases
options.B: Both variables decrease at the exact same time
options.C: Both variables increase at the exact same time
options.D: There is no relationship found between the variables

explanation: Think of it like a seesaw: in a negative correlation, as one variable goes up, the other goes down. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the medical term for difficult or abnormal labour?

options.A: Eutocia
options.B: Inversion
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Dystocia

explanation: Great job! Dystocia simply means labour isn't progressing smoothly. Think of 'eu-' as normal and 'dys-' as difficult. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h1)
